clue.text: Exercise round track for a heavenly body!

indicators.note: round says the exercise letters go around the track word

parts.note: PT, physical training, is the usual abbreviation for exercise
a lane is a narrow track or road

explanation.surface: A runner does laps of a track and somehow ends up among the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Planets such as Mars or Venus are classic examples of heavenly bodies orbiting a star.

clue.text: Agent says Emir's corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or debased, telling us to jumble the preceding letters

parts.note: the word emir is the fodder; its 's stands for 'is', joining fodder to indicator

explanation.surface: An informant reports that a Gulf ruler is on the take.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a person sent on a mission as a representative, which is a kind of agent.

clue.text: Keen for dentist to be prepared before going in

indicators.note: going in says the word for before is placed inside the jumbled letters
something to be prepared is to be made ready or put together, so the letters of dentist are rearranged

parts.note: ere is an old poetic word for before

explanation.surface: An eager patient waits for the dentist to get ready before being called in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dentist' reads as a person but is just fodder; 'to be prepared' shuffles it and 'going in' puts the old word for before inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen on a thing is drawn to it and curious about it, i.e. showing interest.

clue.text: Fairly abrupt exit

indicators.note: abrupt means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: quite means fairly, as in quite good

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a room rather suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit a job or place is to leave it, the same as to quit it.

clue.text: Words that describe these times and aims lose old boy

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the present era of the calendar

indicators.note: lose says the old boy letters are dropped from the word for aims

parts.note: objectives are aims or goals
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about modern times and goals, with a former pupil leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, describing words that qualify nouns, such as red or tall, form a word class with this name.

clue.text: China is aiding part of uprising here

indicators.note: uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Beijing is lending support to a rebellion in this region.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uprising' reads the hidden run AISA from the bottom up; 'here' points to the continent where China lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's 'here' points to the continent containing China, so the place meant is that landmass.

clue.text: Drop long working title

indicators.note: working means being worked over or reshaped, so the letters of title are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer abandons the lengthy working title of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop, as in just a drop of milk, is a small amount, and so is a little.

clue.text: British want Bond in formal attire

parts.note: want in the sense of need or lack
a tie is a bond, as in family ties

explanation.surface: A British agent wants James Bond dressed for a formal evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner jackets with bow ties make up the dress code printed on formal evening invitations.

clue.text: Spread in French newspaper abridged arresting copper's side

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the shortened paper contains the next letters
abridged means shortened, so the paper's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading Paris daily
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
R, for right, is one side

explanation.surface: A shortened Paris newspaper report about a policeman being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arresting' puts CU and R inside LEMOND.
explanation.definitionFit: This citrus-flavoured preserve is spread on toast or scones, like jam.

clue.text: Fall sick after swamp's drained

indicators.note: after says the word for sick follows the two remaining swamp letters
drained means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer letters of swamp

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone falls ill after a marsh is drained.
explanation.definitionFit: A spill is a tumble or fall, as from a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: It's not difficult reviewing issue with lunch

indicators.note: reviewing is read as looking back, so the word for issue is reversed

parts.note: a son is issue, meaning offspring
to lunch is to eat

explanation.surface: A critic finds it easy to review an issue over lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrase is said when a task needed no effort at all.

clue.text: Peel a sticker found inside stretchy material

indicators.note: found inside says the answer sits within the letters of the words that come before

explanation.surface: Peel off a label and discover the springy fabric beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy material of this kind, used in waistbands, springs back to its shape.

clue.text: Leaves note with key

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A departure, noted and keyed in like a message.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose dried leaves of this plant are brewed in a pot, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: English country squire's retaining American realtor

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, so the American letter is kept within

parts.note: a state is a country or nation
a squire is a gentleman, informally a gent

explanation.surface: An English landed gentleman with an American partner, all property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'realtor' is the American word for the British house seller.
explanation.definitionFit: A realtor in the US sells houses on commission, which is what the British property dealer does.

clue.text: Said no to decreased volume

definitions.meaning: lowered the sound on a radio by moving the knob

explanation.definitionFit: An offer that is refused is rejected, and a stereo knob rotated lower plays more quietly.

clue.text: Royal Engineers leave main unit more shot, bullets, shells etc

indicators.note: leave says the engineers' letters are taken out of the pool of letters
shot means ruined or broken up, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers walk away from a main unit after more shots are fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' takes RE out of MAINUNITMORE and 'shot' scrambles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Projectiles and the cartridges that fire them, collectively, make up a weapon's supply.

clue.text: Hear way in which lovers meet

parts.note: a judge who hears a case tries it
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Listen to the route by which romantic couples come together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret romantic rendezvous, the appointment in which a couple meet.

clue.text: Experiment without stress in lesson

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the word for experiment

parts.note: a trial is an experiment or test

indicators.note: stress is taken as strain or deform, so the out letters are rearranged

parts.note: read as with plus out: the out part is the fodder, the with joining it

explanation.surface: A teacher conducts an experiment that keeps the class free of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'without' as 'with out': 'stress' turns OUT into UTO, and 'in' places that inside the experiment word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a teaching session with a tutor, so it is a lesson.

clue.text: Vicar's retiring very shortly

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters are read backwards
shortly means cut short, so the word very loses its last letter

explanation.surface: The clergyman is about to retire very soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims VERY to VER and 'retiring' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title and informal name for a clergyman.

clue.text: Old lady regularly sizzles corn on the cob

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old lady

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of sizzles is taken

explanation.surface: Mum's cobs sizzle on the barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: This cereal is the American corn, eaten whole as corn on the cob.

clue.text: Enduring setter's Monday test — entertaining time?

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so setter's means I am, I'm

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the test word holds the time letter

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam or test

explanation.surface: The setter wonders whether a Monday quiz is a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter referring to themselves gives 'I am'; 'entertaining' puts T inside the spoken test.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enduring lasts forever, like an undying reputation.

clue.text: Husband intercepted pints order sent out for someone else

indicators.note: intercepted means caught in transit, so the husband letter sits among the others
sent out means dispatched in disarray, so the letters of pints and order are rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband snatches a drinks order meant for another drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' scrambles PINTSORDER; 'intercepted' puts H in among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this term refers to people other than the speaker or listener, such as he or she.

clue.text: Half of skin round jab filling with purple colour

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the jab word sits within the others
half of takes the second half of the letters of skin

parts.note: O is round in shape
a dig is a jab or poke

explanation.surface: A nurse jabs skin with a dye that turns it violet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' keeps the back half of skin; 'filling' puts the jab word between that and the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet dye and hue, between blue and violet in the rainbow.

clue.text: Might perhaps be out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the be letters are taken away

parts.note: maybe means perhaps

explanation.surface: Strength could possibly be gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like the noun power; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As modal verbs both express possibility, as in it might rain.

clue.text: During holiday set up child with crafts

indicators.note: during means within, so the child letters go inside
set up in a down clue means read from bottom up, so the letters reverse

parts.note: a stay is a holiday visit

explanation.surface: On holiday a child is set up with crafts to keep busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the holiday word to YATS and 'During' puts the child letters inside; 'crafts' means boats, not hobbies.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafts can mean boats or vessels, and yachts are sailing vessels.

clue.text: Embarrassed about route used to dismiss player

parts.note: embarrassed people go red
CA, circa, means about
RD, road, is a route

explanation.surface: Red-faced about the route taken by a sent-off footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: In football (soccer) a referee shows a player this to send them off.
explanation.definitionFit: Football referees hold up this card to send a player off the field.

clue.text: Log initially cut to hold wheel rod

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the cut word holds the letter

parts.note: to axe is to cut

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of log is used

explanation.surface: Chop a log to make a rod for a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the shaft or spindle on which wheels turn.

clue.text: Mocking luxurious hotel abandoned after located on island

indicators.note: after says the trimmed luxurious word follows the other pieces

parts.note: sat means situated or located

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the hotel letter is dropped

parts.note: rich means luxurious
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mocking the luxury hotel deserted after it was sited on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiric writing ridicules and mocks its targets.

clue.text: Lively ferret about to go under front of sofa

indicators.note: to go under in a down clue means the snooping word goes below the first letter
front of means only the first letter of sofa is used

parts.note: to ferret about is to pry or snoop

explanation.surface: A lively ferret scrambles about under the sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone active and nimble, especially when elderly.

clue.text: High-class new hair product's dear

parts.note: A means first class or top quality
gel is a hair product

explanation.surface: A new upmarket hair product is expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' looks like expensive; it is an endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a dear or a darling is a sweet term of endearment.

clue.text: Labour over wind sculpture

parts.note: work means labour
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
fart is slang for breaking wind

explanation.surface: Effort put into creating a piece of art in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpture is an example of a creative piece of art.
